explanations.explanation: This neuron is a “new‐section/document start” detector—it spikes on the blank‐line/header tokens that mark the very beginning of a text block (titles, section breaks, leading newlines) across all these diverse document formats.

This neuron fires on the single “pivot” token at the head of a clause or title—typically the main content word (a 3rd-person verb like gets, gives, urging, offering, wins, etc., a gerund or noun head like stage or javelin, or a section/part number). In short, it marks the syntactic-semantic head of news-style headlines and headings.

This feature fires on common word-final subword strings—i.e. suffix-like letter sequences (e.g. “azi,” “party,” “its,” “ves,” “ames,” “ains,” “get,” “ages,” “layer,” “iques,” etc.) that regularly occur at the ends of English words.

This feature is essentially a detector for the full‐stop at the end of formal, declarative statements—sentence- or section-final periods in technical/professional prose (e.g. patent claims, headings, headers, blog update titles, copyright notices, etc.).
